motivation: The Qwen3-8B v0.2 run scored 0.167 mean initial individual accuracy under full information, below the 0.8 eligibility gate. The project has a cached, previously runnable Qwen3-14B Q4_K_M checkpoint; screen it before deciding whether to spend on full multi-agent episodes.
question: Does Qwen3-14B reach at least 0.8 mean individual accuracy on initial votes when all HiddenBench facts are visible?

model.name: Qwen3-14B-Q4_K_M
model.runtime: llama.cpp b11202 on RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8 GB; 24 GPU layers with CPU offload; one slot; context 8192; temperature 0; reasoning off

design.scoring: Mean fraction of four initial agent votes matching each task's gold answer, averaged over the three tasks; report the total correct vote count and per-task values. This is the pre-discussion full-profile capability gate used in v0.1/v0.2.

prediction: A stronger same-family checkpoint may improve full-information vote accuracy relative to the Qwen3-8B v0.2 baseline (2/12); no minimum improvement is assumed beyond the 0.8 eligibility gate.
decision_rule: If mean initial individual accuracy is below 0.8, do not run a communication-protocol comparison on this model/task pairing. If it reaches or exceeds 0.8, that only licenses a separately preregistered full HiddenBench calibration; it is not evidence of communication superiority.
limits: Only 12 deterministic votes across three public verification tasks.
This is a model/task capability screen and a paired descriptive comparison with Qwen3-8B, not a causal scaling study.
No discussion, hidden-profile run, or protocol comparison is included.
